title: Meter-Based Energy Classes Reward Underheating: Improving the Energy Performance Assessment of Buildings in Uzbekistan with a Calibration-Based Energy Passport
content: Since 2024, Uzbekistan assigns energy efficiency classes A–G to buildings by comparing metered consumption with the normative value of the national standard ShNQ 2.01.18-24. This study tests whether this rule reflects the thermal quality of buildings. Of 30 audited public buildings, mostly uninsulated and built in 1963–2007, 18 were rated A or B, although 21 were underheated by more than 30%. The index correlated with the degree of underheating (r = −0.83), and the audited demand at comfort conditions would have placed 21 buildings in class F or G. Unspecified accounting choices moved individual buildings across up to all seven classes. We propose a three-stage passport: design calculation, calibration of the heat loss coefficient against daily meter data with an energy signature, and recalculation under standard conditions. For a new house in Tashkent with two years of daily gas readings, the as-built heat loss coefficient was 885 W/K (95% interval 807–978 W/K), 8% above the design value. Metered-use variants placed the house in classes B, D and F, whereas the calibrated passport yielded class C (−24%), and calibrations on either season differed by only 3 points. Separating envelope quality from operation makes meter-informed passports reproducible.
